hypothesis: Repeating polls while the progress counter increases cuts owner ticks without exceeding the controller FIFO budget.
conclusion: This shows the removed per-step tick waits, not physical bus time.
narrative: checks/radio-poll-batching.py (removed from the repository as a one-off radio composition) ran the setup and bootstrap identity sequence of the integrated fixture twice: once with one poll per owner tick and once repeating polls while progress increases. Every call stayed within the controller's FIFO budget, and every repeated tick ended on a waiting call. The fixture's controller model completes bus work instantly, so only the owner's tick count is meaningful: 172 ticks dropped to 42.

hypothesis: The transport works with the real controller, enumeration and codec implementations, including multi-record aggregates, backpressure and fault retention.
conclusion: The integrated transport passed on the host model; no board operation.
narrative: checks/aic8800-sdio-transport.py and checks/radio-transport-aggregate.py (both removed; composition covered by aic8800-dispatch and aic8800-data) built the transport with the real controller, enumeration and codec implementations under address and undefined-behavior sanitizers, reusing the existing register model without running that model's independent suite. The integrated fixture covered: delayed function readiness, block-size verification, preserved enable bits, both pad choices and the required settling interval; credit backpressure, two identity reads, fixed FIFO addressing, zero transmit padding and retained unrelated responses before a matching confirmation; a 10-block aggregate holding three 1,500-byte records before the setup-write confirmation, which starts at byte 4,512, read by one CMD53 of all 5,120 bytes with a deadline of two command timeouts, every record parsed in order; a byte-mode length over 512 bytes, an unsupported interrupt reason, a malformed byte-mode response, a partial FIFO failure and a setup write that takes effect before failure; deadline expiry while waiting for credit or holding an unrelated message, with retained state and no backend access after fault. The aggregate check ran the same model after runtime start with the native dispatcher as receive owner: one CMD53 read an 18-block aggregate holding three 1,500-byte data records, a 4,604-byte print record and an unrelated control message, and the dispatcher retired all five in order and kept a diagnostic copy of the print record truncated to 4,096 bytes. A focused bootstrap integration case passed after adding the fixed memory write: an unrelated response, a write confirmation with non-echo fields, conditional pad restoration, settling and both identity reads, plus malformed/truncated write confirmations, missing confirmation after a modeled write effect, an uncertain pad write and partial transmit failure. The changed codec and transport compiled for freestanding AArch64 (aarch64/results.json records both object identities; runtime dependency beyond the native SDIO/codec APIs is memset). Controller, card and unaffected codec-path evidence was reused. No board operation, firmware selection, performance run or unchanged component-suite rerun was performed.
